name: ground_d
prompt:
Two images are attached. The first is a layout: 12 equal squares in a 4×3 grid on a flat magenta background. The second shows finished art from the same top-down 2D city game: roofs and cars, and on the right a square of the game's old grass. Match that art's look, a little more painterly than the old grass: crisp hand-painted game art, clean confident brushwork, every small shape sharp and readable, natural colours. It must NOT look like a photograph: no blur, no photographic noise, no fine speckle mush.

Make one image with exactly the same 4×3 layout as the first image. Fill each square with the patch of ground described for that cell below: a ground texture the game repeats over large areas under the roofs and cars.

Shape comes first:
- Each square is filled edge to edge, right into all four corners, and stops exactly at its outline. Paint over the outline itself: the finished square has no border, frame, rim, bevel, outline, shadow or vignette, and its edges are as bright and as busy as its middle.
- Draw nothing outside the squares. Outside them, keep the background fully transparent. No text, numbers, labels or grid lines anywhere.

How each square is built, as the old grass is: a calm, smooth painted base with gentle broad variation in its tone, and on it, scattered at random and spaced apart, distinct readable painted details, each crisp-edged, with about a third of the square left as calm base between them. Not a uniform noise of tiny specks.

Rules for every cell:
- Look straight down (orthographic). No perspective, no horizon, no light falling off towards any edge.
- Each square is 9.2 × 9.2 m of ground. Keep everything true to size: a grass tuft about 30 cm across, a flower cluster the size of a hand, an earth patch at most half a metre, a ripple a few tens of centimetres.
- No direction and no pattern: details point every way and are scattered at random, never in rows, stripes, lines or a grid, so the square looks the same turned any way.
- Even texture: the same tone and the same density of detail all over the square; no single detail bigger or brighter than the rest, no blotch, path, puddle, shadow or object, so the square repeats without anything catching the eye.
- Squares that share a description are the same ground: draw them in exactly the same colours, density and style, as different patches of one lawn or one river, so they can be joined without a visible seam.
- Nothing stands on the ground: no trees, bushes, rocks, litter, cars, people, kerbs, markings or lines.

Cells, left to right, top to bottom:

Row 1 — cells 1, 2, 3, 4: a kept town lawn. Base a fresh mid green; small grass tufts drawn as a few crisp blades fanning out, in lighter and darker greens; a little clover; a very few tiny white daisy clusters; only the odd tiny earth spot.

Row 2 — cells 5, 6, 7, 8: the same lawn worn and drier. Base a softer olive green, not yellow; tufts in olive and straw; more small bare brown earth patches; a few tiny yellow flower clusters. Clearly the same grass as row 1, only more worn.

Row 3 — cells 9 and 10: still river water: deep blue-green, small soft painted ripples a few tens of centimetres across, curving every way, a very few small pale glints.
Row 3 — cells 11 and 12: livelier river water: the same deep blue-green a touch lighter and greener, more broken small ripples curving every way, more small pale glints.
